question: Can historical accuracy and correlated pollster forecast errors be combined?
answer: Yes as an optional experimental risk-minimizing method; evidence insufficient for a proven improvement or current full covariance calibration.

recommendedOptionalMethod.target: Minimize w transpose M w, with weights >=0 and sum(weights)=1
recommendedOptionalMethod.diagonal: Election-balanced forecast-error MSE shrunk toward pooled prior with 3 prior elections
recommendedOptionalMethod.offDiagonal: Matched same-party/same-election final forecast-error cross-products; retain biases; shrink heavily toward diagonal
recommendedOptionalMethod.continuity: Transfer only documented historical entities; Lazar attenuation .5. Never assign legacy Direct/Panels/Fuchs errors automatically to new institutes.
recommendedOptionalMethod.unknownPairs: Unknown, not proven independent. Do not market their apparent optimizer advantage as additional information.
recommendedOptionalMethod.implementationGate: Expand matched verified histories/horizons; preregister transfer and shrinkage; chronological withheld-election tests; probability calibration separately; source coverage exposed; base default remains historical quality.

whyNotVIF: Classical VIF measures regression coefficient instability from collinear predictors. Forecast combination directly optimizes error-risk; applying VIF to raw party seat/share vectors mistakes the common political signal and sum-to-120 composition for redundant errors.

references.title: Bates and Granger (1969), The Combination of Forecasts
references.role: Past forecast errors determine combination weights; publisher abstract read on 2026-10-09.

references.title: Elliott (2011), Averaging and the Optimal Combination of Forecasts
references.role: Author paper: covariance-based combination, estimation error, common error and nonnegative restrictions; pages 1–10 reviewed.

references.title: Ledoit and Wolf (2004), A well-conditioned estimator for large-dimensional covariance matrices
references.role: Primary publisher abstract on covariance shrinkage; the fixed 75% coefficient used here is OUR assumption, not the Ledoit–Wolf estimated coefficient.

references.title: statsmodels variance_inflation_factor documentation
references.role: Official documentation: VIF is a linear-regression coefficient variance/multicollinearity diagnostic, not itself a forecast-weight formula.

assertions: All selected final published seat vectors and actual outcomes sum to 120.
Independent active-subset quadratic solver reproduces archived 2022 equal/accuracy/dependence metrics and weights.
Each chronological test election is excluded from its weight calculations.
Output weights are nonnegative and sum to 1.
Synthetic correlated duplicate forecasts lose individual weight.
A uniform shared-error risk floor leaves weights unchanged and remains in aggregate risk.
